Additional comments:

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really easy. In Norway they have a whole housing unit for students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You get to explorer more and get a mental break from Uni.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You already get registreted through the learning agreement. You just have to get a study card. they guide you very well on how to get things done. they have a informational reception at every faculty.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help with Uni and technical stuff. Help with changeing courses if you change your mind.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read your e-mails,

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.answer: Very satisfying level. But that also depends on which level you take your courses.

questions.answer: It was very much alike, but all the lectures were held at real lecture halls and not in classrooms where most of my lectures have been.

questions.answer: Courses you find interesting. I would reccomed all of the courses i had cause they were really interesting and i completed them with a feeling of having learning much that i can apply in further studies.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were movie"nights"  at campus. and the gyms were also very close to campus, there were even one located at campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definately, do the Atletica gym if youre going to Norway. Its cheap and you have acces to different team training like step, yoga, boxing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Make friends at school or your gym at go out and explore the city and other towns of Norway
Theres board game cafees for people that like to do something chill.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Im from Denmark and went to Norway.
I could understand norwegian and most of the times the could understand me. 
Very easy to adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sit beside them in lectures and ask about local stuff and they will proberbly offer to show you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: i love different cultures. I didnt find anything challening cause im a very openminded person. But norwegian student dont open up that easy or talk as regularly as danish people. So you have to be consistent,

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the calm and helpful nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared, read your mails.
Dont be afraid- be in control of your actions.
Go with studyng in mind and as your priority but have fun in weekends at the same time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have 4 hour school exams in norway. You need adapt your study habits according to the exams. Always read about the exam and how it goes on the course information page.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Leaving with a feeling of accomplishing what i went for: knowlegde of specific themes aka my courses. And i got friends for life aswell, through the gym and Uni.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting too attached to the place.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
